title: Pipe renewals under spread budgets

blocks.text: This is the whiteboard question of the mock, coded. A water utility's model in `renewals.py` already has a start variable `x[(rid, year)]` for each renewal and each year in its window, the row that each renewal starts at most once, and an objective. Three of the interviewer's rules are missing:

items: **Budgets.** A renewal spends `cost[0]` in its start year, `cost[1]` the next year, and so on. In every year of `budgets`, the renewals' spend in that year is at most the budget.
**Predecessors.** A renewal with a `parent` may start in year $`t`$ only if the parent was funded and started in a year $`s \le t - \text{lag}`$.
**Alternatives.** Renewals that share a `group` are alternatives for one main: at most one of them is funded, whatever years they would start in.

blocks.text: Write `add_rules(model, x, renewals, budgets)` so the model allows exactly the plans that keep all three. Write your formulation first, in the notation of the mock's whiteboard (sets, parameters, variables with domains, each row with its quantifier and a label), then code it. A year in which nothing can be spent has an empty sum: in Python that is the number 0, not a row, so write no row for it.
The tests fix a plan through the variables' bounds and ask HiGHS whether the model allows it, so any correct formulation passes. About twenty lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Renewal:
    rid: str
    starts: tuple[int, ...]            # the years it may start in
    cost: tuple[int, ...]              # $k spent in its first, second, ... year of work
    value: int = 10
    parent: str | None = None          # may start only `lag` years after this renewal starts
    lag: int = 0                       # start to start, in years
    group: str | None = None           # alternatives for one main share a group


def start_variables(model: mathopt.Model, renewals: list[Renewal]) -> dict:
    """x[(rid, year)] = 1 when the renewal starts in that year; only years in its window exist."""
    return {(r.rid, t): model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{r.rid}_{t}") for r in renewals for t in r.starts}


def add_once_rows(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, renewals: list[Renewal]) -> None:
    """Given: each renewal starts at most once."""
    for r in renewals:
        model.add_linear_constraint(sum(x[r.rid, t] for t in r.starts) <= 1, name=f"once_{r.rid}")


def add_rules(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, renewals: list[Renewal], budgets: dict[int, int]) -> None:
    """The budget of every year, every predecessor with its lag, and every alternative group."""
    # TODO: write the formulation's rows here.
    return None


def build(renewals: list[Renewal], budgets: dict[int, int]) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="pipe-renewals")
    x = start_variables(model, renewals)
    add_once_rows(model, x, renewals)
    add_rules(model, x, renewals, budgets)
    model.maximize(sum(r.value * x[r.rid, t] for r in renewals for t in r.starts))
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mains = [Renewal("R1", (2027, 2028), (40, 40)), Renewal("R2", (2028,), (30,), parent="R1", lag=1)]
    model, x = build(mains, {2027: 50, 2028: 50})
    print(len(list(model.linear_constraints())), "rows")

cases.says: a plan within every year's budget is allowed, and one that overspends a year is refused
one alternative for a main is allowed, and two in the same year are refused
a child that starts well after its parent is allowed, and one that starts too soon is refused
each year is charged only what the renewals spend in that year, not their whole cost in the start year
two alternatives for one main are refused even when they start in different years
a child may start exactly its lag after its parent
a child whose parent is not funded is refused
